records.request:
Produce one ultra-high-fidelity photographic edit of Image 1: a candid Nantucket summer family moment, with restrained slow-shutter subject motion and an unchanged architectural setting.

INPUT ROLES
The single attached image is the property photograph and immutable base plate. Edit this exact photograph in place. It is not inspiration for a new room. Preserve its original composition and every existing structural element. The desired aesthetic is crisp real-estate architecture with softly moving candid people.

1. IMMUTABLE PROPERTY PLATE
Preserve Image 1 exactly: camera position, wide-angle perspective, full frame, room proportions, straight lines, architecture, doors, windows, staircase and railings, fixtures, existing furniture, artwork and lettering, landscaping, pool geometry, daylight direction, exposure and color grade. Add people and a few appropriate movable props only. Never crop, zoom, redesign, relight or replace the property. Architecture remains the hero, tack-sharp and unobstructed enough to evaluate.

2. SCENE INTENT
Evocate an intimate Nantucket summer gathering. In kitchen/dining/living spaces, two to four adults or family members share a modest charcuterie-and-cheese board, sourdough, grapes or farm tomatoes; a couple of adults may hold small glasses of pale rose or white wine, children have lemonade. If there is enough table space in a dining setting, lobster rolls and sweet corn may replace the board. At the pool, two adults settle into nautical lounge seating with a small snack side table, children nearby only with an attentive adult. Closet/stairs show one fully dressed adult getting ready to join the gathering, without food props there.

3. ADAPT TO THE VISIBLE SPACE
Infer the actual space from Image 1 and choose ONE believable activity. Game room: a parent and child playing the existing table-tennis table with a clear playing lane. Kitchen/bar: preparing or passing a light summer snack at the existing counter. Dining room: sharing food at the existing table. Living room: reading, conversation or a simple family game using existing seating. Pool/deck/garden: relaxing together, a parent supervising a child, or carrying folded towels; if the deck is empty, add only two or three teak or woven lounge/director chairs with cream or navy-striped cushions and one small side table, placed in physically open space. Closet: one fully dressed adult choosing a shirt or sunhat; keep the adjoining bathroom empty. Stairs/hall: one or two people carefully passing through, a hand naturally near the rail. A vintage pale sage or cream 1966–77 Ford Bronco with a white top may appear ONLY if an actual driveway/garage parking surface is visible; never put a vehicle on a lawn, pool deck or inside a home. Do not invent another location or force every motif into one photograph.

4. CAST AND WARDROBE
Classic Nantucket summer, relaxed and lived-in: airy white or pale-blue linen, soft Oxford cotton, navy-and-ivory boatneck stripes, khaki shorts, a single faded salmon Nantucket Reds accent when appropriate, simple sundresses, canvas sneakers, boat shoes or flat sandals. Real people with natural varied faces, ages and body types, loose hair and unforced posture; coordinated palette without identical matching outfits. Bare feet only where natural. No nautical costume, conspicuous logos or fashion-campaign posing. Keep everyone occupied with one another, not looking into the lens. Children are school-age, in ordinary age-appropriate summer clothing; any wine is held only by adults.

5. PHOTOGRAPHIC MOTION
Keep the people delicately motion-softened, like a candid slow-shutter hospitality photo: a turning head, hand offering a plate or wine glass and linen hem show a short natural directional blur. Table surfaces, food at rest and all original architectural detail stay crisp. Avoid a frozen stock-photo toast.

6. INTEGRATION
Match the source light, white balance and grain. Add correct scale, perspective, grounded feet, contact shadows, plausible reflections, natural occlusion behind chairs and railings, and anatomically coherent hands. Preserve the original foreground and sense of spaciousness. Newly added stationary props stay sharp. No duplicated people, transparent ghosts, doubled limbs, smeared faces, global blur, artificial bokeh, CGI gloss, added text or watermark.

Deliver only the edited full-frame photograph. Resolve conflicts in favor of preserving Image 1 and physically plausible, restrained staging.
